questions.question: Which protocol is listed under the OSI Presentation layer?

options.A: POP

questions.explanation: Presentation layer protocols are MIME and NCP (NetWare Core Protocol); PPTP is Session, SLIP Data Link, POP Application.

questions.question: Which condition must the list satisfy before binary search can be applied?

options.A: It must have an odd number of elements
options.C: It must contain only positive numbers
options.D: It must have no duplicate elements

questions.explanation: Binary search relies on the ordering of elements, so the list must be sorted (ascending, descending or alphabetical).

questions.concept: Match the Sum valid selection of digits
questions.question: In the 'Match the Sum' game, the displayed cells include the digits 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7. Which typed selection would be accepted and removed?
questions.explanation: A student may type 2 or 3 displayed digits whose sum is 10; 3 + 7 = 10. The selection 1, 2, 3, 4 sums to 10 but uses four digits, 4 + 7 = 11 and 2 + 3 + 6 = 11.

questions.question: A student types select * from STUDENT; instead of SELECT * FROM STUDENT;. How does SQL treat these keywords?

options.A: SQL is case insensitive, so both forms work
options.C: Mixed case gives a syntax error

questions.explanation: SQL is case insensitive for its keywords, so select and SELECT are treated the same.

questions.concept: Classifying DES and RSA by key usage
questions.question: With algorithm X, both parties must share one secret key in advance. With algorithm Y, anyone can encrypt using a widely shared key and only the owner's private key can decrypt. X and Y are respectively:

options.A: RSA and DES

questions.explanation: DES is a conventional symmetric-key algorithm (single shared secret key) and RSA is the classic asymmetric public-key algorithm.

questions.question: Which pairing of memory type and its inventor/founder is correct?

options.A: EPROM: Dov Frohman; EEPROM: Robert Heath Dennard
options.B: EPROM: Dov Frohman; EEPROM: Fujio Masuoka
options.C: EPROM: Robert Heath Dennard; EEPROM: Dov Frohman
options.D: EPROM: Fujio Masuoka; EEPROM: Dov Frohman

questions.explanation: Dov Frohman invented EPROM and Fujio Masuoka is the founder of EEPROM. Robert Heath Dennard is credited with DRAM.

questions.concept: Encapsulation as binding versus abstraction as hiding
questions.question: Encapsulation and abstraction are best distinguished as:

options.A: Encapsulation is hiding; abstraction is binding
options.B: Both are forms of code reuse through derivation
options.C: Both describe one name taking many forms
options.D: Encapsulation is binding; abstraction is hiding

questions.explanation: Encapsulation binds data and its functions into one unit, while abstraction hides implementation details. Reuse through derivation is inheritance and many forms is polymorphism.

questions.concept: Build and Fix not suitable for large complex work
questions.question: A team proposes to build a large, highly complex hospital management system using the Build and Fix model. What is the main objection to this choice?

options.A: It requires a formal risk analysis in every cycle
options.B: It is not suitable for large or highly complex work
options.C: It needs users to be involved in every phase
options.D: It forces a separate test phase for every development phase

questions.explanation: Build and Fix suits only small programs and is not suitable for large or highly complex work. The other options describe the V-model, spiral model and prototyping respectively.

questions.concept: RISC high-end vs CISC low-end applications
questions.question: Which statement correctly matches architectures with their typical applications?

options.A: CISC suits high-end uses like image processing; RISC suits low-end uses like home automation
options.B: EPIC suits low-end uses like security systems; CISC suits telecommunications
options.C: RISC and CISC are both limited to low-end uses like security systems
options.D: RISC suits high-end uses like image processing; CISC suits low-end uses like home automation

questions.explanation: RISC is used in high-end applications (video/image processing, telecommunications); CISC in low-end applications (security systems, home automation).

questions.question: Which limitation applies to statements typed in Python's interactive mode?

options.A: They cannot be saved for future use
options.B: They cannot display the result of an expression
options.C: They can contain only arithmetic expressions
options.D: They must be compiled before execution

questions.explanation: Interactive mode is convenient for instantly testing single-line code, but those statements cannot be saved for later; script mode (.py files) is used for that.

questions.question: Which expression correctly represents the 'equation' of the Internet of Things?

options.A: Physical object + controller, sensor and actuator + Internet

questions.explanation: IoT = Physical Object + Controller, Sensor and Actuator + Internet. The other options drop one or more essential parts.

questions.question: How does steganography differ from encryption?

options.A: It converts plaintext to ciphertext; encryption hides data in images
options.B: It uses a public-private key pair; encryption uses one secret key
options.C: It protects only passwords; encryption protects only stored files
options.D: It embeds hidden data in media; encryption transforms data into an obscure form

questions.explanation: Steganography hides data by embedding it (for example inside an image), whereas encryption transforms the data into an unreadable format.

questions.concept: First robot on General Motors assembly line
questions.question: In which year was the first robot introduced to the General Motors assembly line?
questions.explanation: The first robot joined the GM assembly line in 1960. 1956 is the coining of AI, 1961 is ELIZA, and 1953 is listed for machine learning.

questions.concept: Turing machine as model of a general-purpose computer
questions.question: Which machine is described as a theoretical model of a general-purpose computer, capable of solving any computable problem?

options.A: Pushdown automata

questions.explanation: The Turing machine is the theoretical model of a general-purpose computer and the most powerful of the primary machines.

questions.question: Using a stack, what is the value of the postfix expression 5 1 2 + 4 * + 3 - ?
questions.explanation: 1 2 + = 3; 3 4 * = 12; 5 12 + = 17; 17 3 - = 14. Reversing the operand order for '-' would wrongly give -14.

questions.question: A small representation of a larger image, often used for previews, is called a:

options.A: Watermark

questions.explanation: A thumbnail is a small preview version of a larger image; a pixel is the smallest picture element, not a preview.

questions.concept: Shell as interface between user and OS
questions.question: What is the role of a shell in an operating system?

options.A: It schedules processes from the ready queue onto the CPU
options.B: It allocates frames of physical memory to pages
options.C: It takes commands from the user and passes them to the operating system
options.D: It translates logical addresses into physical addresses

questions.explanation: A shell is the interface between the user and the OS: it accepts user commands and hands them to the OS. Examples are sh, csh and ksh.

questions.question: In Python functions, what is a parameter?

options.A: The value passed to the function at the time of the call
options.B: The name used to call the function
options.C: The value returned by the function
options.D: The variable defined in the function header that receives a value

questions.explanation: An argument is the value passed during the call, and a parameter is the variable in the function header that receives it.

questions.question: The Myhill-Nerode theorem, used to minimize states of a DFA, dates from which year?
questions.explanation: The Myhill-Nerode theorem is from 1958; 1936 is the Turing machine year.

questions.question: Which C++ storage specifier requests that a variable be stored in a CPU register rather than RAM?

options.A: Automatic

questions.explanation: The register specifier allocates memory in a register instead of RAM. Automatic is the default for locals, static persists until program end, and mutable allows change after creation.

questions.concept: Doubly linked list for undo and redo
questions.question: Which type of linked list is cited as being used for Undo and Redo operations?

options.A: Doubly linked list

questions.explanation: A doubly linked list can move both backward (undo) and forward (redo). Circular linked lists are cited for Round Robin CPU scheduling.

questions.question: In disk scheduling, what does SSTF stand for?

options.A: Shortest Service Time First

questions.explanation: SSTF is Shortest Seek Time First; other disk algorithms include FCFS, SCAN, C-SCAN, LOOK and C-LOOK.

questions.question: Which group contains only lossy formats?

options.A: GIF, BMP, WAV

questions.explanation: JPEG, MP3 and MPEG are lossy; PNG, FLAC, GIF, BMP and WAV are lossless.

questions.question: A network accessible only to the employees of an organisation is called:

options.A: Extranet

questions.explanation: Internet is open to all, Intranet is only for employees and Extranet is shared between two companies.

questions.question: Firebase, listed among DBMS software, is associated with which company?

options.A: Google

questions.explanation: Firebase is Google's database platform; Amazon offers DynamoDB and Microsoft offers SQL Server and Access.
